header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Platform: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Lynx Head of Ops), Tom Becker (Lynx SRE), Nina Patel (Lynx Security), Jared Lin (Lynx PM)
Context: Weekly POC sync focused on security/compliance items (SSO, audit logs, data retention), quick results review, tuning notes, and concrete next steps.
summary: This weekly check-in focused on closing open security questions for the Lynx systems pilot. Main threads: SSO metadata exchange and preferred IdP flow, audit log granularity and export cadence, retention window options and PII handling, and a short review of preliminary latency/cost numbers. Action items assigned for SOC2 docs, benchmark run, and retention confirmation. Agreed to a SAML metadata deep-dive next week.
topics: SSO / SAML setup and IdP flow
Data retention windows and PII redaction
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everyone I think we're live. thanks for joining this afternoon. quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha Rahman: Hey this is Aisha, here.
[00:08] Tom Becker: Tom here.
[00:09] Nina Patel: Nina on security.
[00:11] Jared Lin: Jared, product.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood, SE.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Cool, thanks. Agenda is short — SSO, audit logs, retention, and then perf numbers diego wanted to show.
[00:22] Aisha Rahman: Sounds good. We're mostly trying to unblock legal and identity for the pilot ramp next week. Key question: can we do SSO with our Okta tenant, and is there a SP-initiated flow option?
[00:30] Diego Alvarez: Yes, Okta is supported. We prefer SP-initiated for console flows but we also support IdP-initiated. There's a SAML metadata file we can ingest. We'll need your IdP cert and entityID.
[00:44] Nina Patel: Ok, on that — does redwood expose metadata at a predictable endpoint or do you send us a file? We have strict change control so we prefer a static metadata url.
[00:53] Diego Alvarez: Right now we can provide a metadata xml hosted on our endpoints for the private plane and hosted. For Dedicated/DC we can host or you can host it. We'll attach the metadata link in the packet; if you need a static host we can pin one for the duration of the pilot.
[01:09] Nina Patel: Great. Also what about session length and token revocation — we need SSO sessions to expire at 8 hours and ability to force logout.
[01:17] Maya Chen: We typically support session TTL config per account. Force logout is supported via the admin console — it signals token revocation to the runtime. Diego: any nuance?
[01:25] Diego Alvarez: The only nuance is for streaming sessions with long-lived websocket tokens there is a gap — but we have an admin endpoint that can break KV cache and invalidate sessions within a minute. It's in the security docs we'll share.
[01:39] Tom Becker: That's fine as long as it's auditable. Which leads to audit logs — what events do you capture by default?
[01:47] Maya Chen: We capture auth/login, token issuance, model inference requests (meta only), admin changes, rollout events, and config changes. We redact prompt content by default in hosted unless customer opts-in.
[01:59] Nina Patel: By 'meta only' do you mean we don't get the actual prompt text in the standard audit logs?
[02:05] Diego Alvarez: Correct. Default audit schema includes user id, request id, model name, token counts, latency, and a classification of whether the prompt contained PII. Prompt text is only in the full request logs and is retained based on retention policy.
[02:20] Nina Patel: Hmm we need both an auditable trail and the ability to pull full request logs if legal asks. What's the retention for full logs?
[02:28] Maya Chen: For the pilot we offered 30, 90, or 365 day retention tiers. Full request logs can be exported to your S3 or kept in our retention store depending on your choice.
[02:39] Aisha Rahman: Our legal leans to 90, but someone on compliance asked about PII redaction. Can redwood redact PII at ingest or do you recommend tokenization on our side?
[02:48] Diego Alvarez: We can do both. There's an ingest redaction pipeline — regex-based and optional ML-based classifier to mask email/SSN patterns. It's best-effort, though we'd recommend front-end tokenization for PHI-level requirements.
[03:02] Nina Patel: Ok put that in writing. We need to see the regex patterns and where masks are applied.
[03:07] Diego Alvarez: Will do, I'll include the config examples.
[03:10] Jared Lin: Quick note — if retention moves to 365, what's the cost delta? We want to weigh it against legal burden.
[03:16] Maya Chen: We'll send a cost delta sheet in the follow-ups — short version, ~2-3x storage costs for 365 over 30 in hosted; export to your S3 reduces storage cost on our side but you keep egress and storage.
[03:29] Tom Becker: About audit export cadence — can we ship logs in near real time to our SIEM? We prefer a streaming export vs daily batch.
[03:36] Diego Alvarez: Yes, near-real-time streaming via Kinesis or GCP Pub/Sub is supported. We guarantee at-least-once delivery; there is a configurable buffer to avoid overloading SIEM.
[03:48] Nina Patel: Anything about log integrity / signing? We need tamper-evidence for audit trail.
[03:54] Maya Chen: We have immutable event sequence numbers and optional log signing with customer-managed KMS. We can sign exports using your KMS key.
[04:04] Nina Patel: Great. Can you point to the doc?
[04:07] Diego Alvarez: Shared doc: redwood.com/security/audit-exports (I'll paste link in the notes).
[04:12] Maya Chen: Pulling the perf numbers now — diego you had a run against 4k context?
[04:17] Diego Alvarez: Yeah quick share. We ran 1k and 4k token synthetic traces with the pilot model (quantized). Median latency at 4k was around 280ms per token for the top-k setting we used, p95 about 1.2s but that's with no KV prefill; if you prewarm the KV cache p95 drops to ~650ms.
[04:37] Tom Becker: That seems okay — our target is p95 under 1s for user facing. Does the p95 include network egress?
[04:43] Diego Alvarez: Includes our platform queuing and runtime compute; network to your region adds ~30-60ms typical.
[04:49] Aisha Rahman: Can we throttle or cap tokens to keep cost predictable?
[04:54] Maya Chen: Yes, we can configure per-route token caps, and you can set per-user quotas in the console. Diego: any tips for cost management?
[05:02] Diego Alvarez: Use prefix caching and prompt templating to reduce repeated tokens; also consider a quantized L2 variant for high-volume non-critical routes. Our optimize module can recommend settings based on the first two weeks of traces.
[05:17] Nina Patel: Back to SOC2 — we requested evidence of scope and last audit date. Do you have a redacted attestation we can share with procurement?
[05:26] Maya Chen: Yes, we will share a redacted SOC2 type II attestation. I'll attach it to the CRM record and email procurement.
[05:33] Nina Patel: Also need encryption at rest details and KMS integration notes.
[05:38] Diego Alvarez: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM for Private installs. Rest encryption uses AES-256. We'll add the key rotation cadence and sample policies.
[05:49] Aisha Rahman: For Private deployment — since we're evaluating an early Dedicated pool, what changes for audit scope? Does dedicated still route through redwood control plane?
[06:00] Maya Chen: For Dedicated, the control plane remains managed but we isolate compute and logs. For Private (VPC or on-prem) you get a private control plane option where audit logs can be kept entirely in your VPC. Diego: correct?
[06:11] Diego Alvarez: Yes — Private deployment gives you the option to host the control plane and logs in your environment. In that model you operate the logging and we provide the same API surface and support package.
[06:21] Tom Becker: Ok makes sense. On the SAML exchange, who should we send metadata to?
[06:25] Maya Chen: Send to maya@redwood.com and diego@redwood.com. We'll ingest and return a signed metadata file.
[06:31] Jared Lin: Question from product — do you have any guardrails for hallucinations or toxicity filtering at the API level? We want to run a reranking pipeline for high-risk outputs.
[06:41] Diego Alvarez: We have post-processing hooks and safety models that can run a classification step. You can run the reranker as an internal microservice or use our built-in safety plugin. It logs the safety decision in the audit entry with the reason code.
[06:54] Aisha Rahman: Great. Are those safety decisions stored indefinitely? We need to make sure they comply with retention.
[07:00] Diego Alvarez: Safety metadata follows the same retention policy as request logs unless configured separately.
[07:06] Nina Patel: Ok need to see schema for that safety metadata.
[07:09] Diego Alvarez: Will include an example JSON schema in the follow-up.
[07:12] Maya Chen: quick checkpoint — any blockers to the pilot continuing?
[07:16] Aisha Rahman: Legal wants SOC2 and a retention decision. Identity needs the metadata and a test account for Okta. Both are blockers for ramp to next week.
[07:25] Nina Patel: Also want PII redact config and evidence of log signing.
[07:29] Maya Chen: We will prioritize that. Diego, can you run the benchmark and share the CSV and charts?
[07:34] Diego Alvarez: Yep I'll run an expanded benchmark with KV prewarm and without; will attach results.
[07:40] Tom Becker: For bench — include both hosted and dedicated latencies if possible, because we want to compare the noise floor.
[07:46] Diego Alvarez: I'll include both.
[07:49] Jared Lin: For analytics — can we capture token-level cost per route in the console for this pilot?
[07:54] Maya Chen: Yes, we have token-level cost breakdown in the console; we'll enable route-level reporting for your account.
[07:59] Aisha Rahman: Any issues with exporting logs to Splunk?
[08:03] Diego Alvarez: Splunk's HEC endpoint is supported. For high throughput we recommend batching at 1s intervals.
[08:11] Nina Patel: A few more quick clarifications — can you confirm data residency options? We need EU region for some teams.
[08:19] Maya Chen: You can pin region at the account level; we have EU regions available for hosted and dedicated. Private on-prem of course stays local.
[08:27] Nina Patel: And the attestation — when was the last audit?
[08:30] Maya Chen: Last Type II audit completed Q4 2025. We'll include the date in the artifact.
[08:36] Aisha Rahman: Ok good. Anything else?
[08:39] Tom Becker: Small thing — can we get a sample SAML metadata response in the next 24 hours so our IdP team can test?
[08:45] Diego Alvarez: Yes I'll send a sample today.
[08:47] Maya Chen: Fine. Recap — Maya will send SOC2 excerpt and the security one-pager; Diego will run bench and send results and SAML sample; Nina will confirm retention preference; schedule SAML metadata deep-dive next week.
[09:01] Aisha Rahman: Thanks all.
[09:03] Nina Patel: thanks.
[09:04] Jared Lin: Thanks team.
[09:06] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and action items.
[09:09] [Recording ends]
